stem: A retailer's legacy-systems team wants to move an existing on-premises Java application into Amazon ECS containers without changing the application's source code.

choices.text: Use AWS Copilot to deploy the application to ECS from a Dockerfile the team writes based on the existing server's dependencies
Rewrite the application as a set of AWS Lambda functions
Use AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) to rehost the application on a new EC2 instance without containerizing it
Use AWS App2Container to analyze the running application and generate the container image and ECS task definition

rationale: AWS App2Container analyzes an application already running on a server, identifies its runtime and dependencies, packages it into a container image, and generates the ECS task definition, all without requiring source code changes, which is exactly the lift-and-shift the team wants. AWS Copilot deploys and operates a containerized application on ECS or Fargate, but it still expects the team to supply a Dockerfile or existing container image; it does not analyze the running server and discover its dependencies the way App2Container does, so the team is back to writing the Dockerfile itself. AWS Application Migration Service rehosts a server onto a new EC2 instance as a lift-and-shift migration, but it does not produce a container image or an ECS task definition, so the application ends up on EC2, not in a container. Leaving the application running unchanged on EC2 does not containerize anything at all, so it does not meet the stated goal either.
